summary: Seychelles is visa-free for every nationality on earth — all visitors receive a Visitor's Permit on arrival for up to three months — but everyone must first obtain the Electronic Travel Authorisation (EUR 10) online before boarding.

passportValidity.text: Seychelles only requires your passport to be valid for the length of your stay, but airlines en route may apply stricter rules — six months' validity avoids problems.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited more than 12 hours through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Seychelles Electronic Border System — official Travel Authorisation portal

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but healthcare for visitors is private and serious cases are evacuated abroad — travel cover including medical evacuation is recommended.

source.name: Seychelles Electronic Border System — official Travel Authorisation portal

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed return or onward ticket is required for the Visitor's Permit and is checked both at check-in and on arrival.

source.name: Seychelles Electronic Border System — official Travel Authorisation portal

proofOfFunds.text: Immigration expects proof of sufficient funds — commonly cited as around USD 150 per person per day — together with confirmed accommodation for the whole stay.

source.name: Seychelles Electronic Border System — official Travel Authorisation portal

currencyLimits.text: Cash above roughly SCR 50,000 (or the foreign-currency equivalent) should be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Seychelles customs before traveling with large amounts.

source.name: Seychelles Electronic Border System — official Travel Authorisation portal

notes: Spearfishing equipment and spear guns may not be brought into Seychelles.
Fruit, vegetables, plants and animal products must be declared and may be seized to protect the islands' ecosystems.

payments.text: Cards are accepted at hotels, restaurants and larger shops, and tourism prices are often quoted (and payable) in euros; keep some rupees for market stalls, buses and small vendors.

safety.text: Seychelles is a safe destination with little serious crime. Petty theft from beaches, rental cars and unattended bungalows is the main issue — use hotel safes — and rip currents deserve real respect: swim where conditions are flagged safe.

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–May and October–November — the calm spells between the trade winds — bring the flattest seas and best visibility for beaches and diving; the islands are warm all year.

idp.text: Seychelles is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Seychelles is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Seychelles yet.

tips.text: Complete the EUR 10 Travel Authorisation at seychelles.govtas.com before check-in — airlines cannot board you without it. Apply once flights and accommodation are booked; standard processing usually takes under 24 hours. Use only the official site.
Every night of your stay must be in licensed, pre-booked accommodation — immigration can ask for the bookings on arrival, so arrange the whole itinerary before you fly.

Rip currents claim lives every year, and conditions shift with the trade-wind seasons — swim at beaches with lifeguards where possible and heed warning flags, especially May to September on south- and west-facing beaches.
Ferries and short flights between Mahé, Praslin and La Digue sell out in high season. Book inter-island transport ahead rather than on the day.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Seychelles?
faq.answer: No — Seychelles is visa-free for every nationality, one of the very few countries in the world with no visa requirement at all. Visitors receive a Visitor's Permit on arrival, normally for the length of the visit up to three months. The only pre-travel step is the EUR 10 Electronic Travel Authorisation, mandatory for everyone.

faq.question: What is the Seychelles Travel Authorisation?
faq.answer: A digital entry clearance applied for at seychelles.govtas.com after you have booked flights and accommodation. It costs EUR 10 per person (including children), is usually approved within hours, and must be shown at check-in — without it, airlines will not board you.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Seychelles?
faq.answer: The Visitor's Permit is issued for the length of your visit, up to three months initially. It can be extended in-country, in stages, up to a maximum of twelve months in total, provided you still have accommodation, funds and an onward ticket.

faq.question: What do I need to show on arrival in Seychelles?
faq.answer: Your approved Travel Authorisation, a passport valid for your stay, a confirmed return or onward ticket, proof of booked accommodation for every night, and evidence of sufficient funds — commonly cited as around USD 150 per person per day.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations for Seychelles?
faq.answer: There are no routine vaccination requirements. A yellow fever certificate is only demanded if you arrive from a country with transmission risk. Seychelles is malaria-free.
